reason: The leaf blade margin is said to be involute. Swapping the blade for its margin is right.
8-12 lateral veins on each side of the midrib of the leaf blade; the count, the bearer and the each-side position are all right.
'Many-flowered inflorescence' does say that flowers are present in the inflorescence, with 'many' kept as the count word.
The corolla is 'pale purplish', so purple marked as approximate is right. 'Pale' is a lightness qualifier only.
The ovary is inserted in the receptacle; 'inserted into' with the receptacle as target matches. 'Obliquely' is a manner that is not captured, but nothing false is said.
'Cymes headlike' means a capitate inflorescence.
'Fleurs ... entourées de 2 bractéoles': 2 bracteoles per flower.
Shrubs or trees 30-50(-80) dm is 300-500 cm, with an extreme of 800 cm. The height of the whole plant is right.
'Shrubs' gives a shrubby (frutescent) habit for the whole plant.

fix: 'hairy outside, glabrous within': 'within', 'inside' and 'inner surface' must fill the place slot (adaxial or inner surface). Without it, 'glabrous' contradicts 'hairy outside' on the same sepal.
reason: The sepals are hairy on the outside and glabrous only on the inside. Saying the whole sepal is glabrous is false.
The plants are up to 1 m tall: an upper bound of 1 m for the height of the whole plant.

fix: In 'not conspicuously X', the 'not' applies to the adverb, not to X. Read it as 'X, inconspicuously' or drop it, never as 'not X'. The bearer would also be better as leaf lamina vein (PO_0020138).
reason: The flora says the veins are reticulate but not conspicuously so; the annotation denies that they are reticulate.

fix: 'about N' should carry an approximate qualifier on the count.
reason: There are about 9 lateral leaf nerves on each side; the count and the position are right. Only the 'about' qualifier is missing.
The anthers are almost entirely adnate to the style arms; the relation and the target are right.

fix: 'bristly' should map to PATO bristly (or setose/hispid), not to the generic pubescent hair. The statement also covers the peduncle.
reason: Bristly hairs are stiff bristles, and PATO has a term for them.
The leaf blade is 4-10 × 1.2-3 cm; the first number range is the length.
'Stamens ... subequal' becomes equal in size, approximately. That is an acceptable reading.
The leaf base is decurrent.
The rhizome is moniliform.
The receptacle shape runs from discoid to broadly turbinate; reading it as a continuum is right. 'Shallowly cup-shaped' is a third step that this record does not cover.
The leaves are flaccid. PATO has no 'flaccid' term, and flexible is the nearest existing quality.

fix: In compound colour names the head word is the last one: 'whitish mineral gray' is gray tending to white, not white.
reason: The thallus is a whitish gray, not white.

target: terminal leaf lamina lobe; place: apex
fix: 'terminal [lobe] broadened at apex' needs both the position slot (terminal lobe) and the place slot (apex). 'Broadened at apex' means the lobe gets wider towards its tip, not that the whole lobe is wider.
reason: Only the terminal lobe is meant, and only at its apex. Without both, the annotation says that all lobes are wider overall.

fix: 'glaucous' should map to PATO glaucous (a waxy bloom), not to an approximate green colour. 'Apically' should fill the place slot, and the bearer should be stem internode (PO_0020142).
reason: The internodes are glaucous at the apex. The green of the annotation comes from 'initially green', not from this statement.

fix: 'subequaling' should carry an approximate qualifier on the 1:1 ratio.
reason: The stamens are about as long as the petals; the length relation to the petals is right.
The apices of the pinnae of the fertile fronds are acuminate; the whole slot (fertile frond) is filled.
'Perennial herbs or shrubs' gives herbaceous or frutescent habit as alternatives.
The berries are red or purple.
The flower buds are long oval-shaped. PATO elliptic lists 'ellipsoid' as a synonym, so it covers this 3D shape.
The costal cells are often smooth: plant cell inside the costa (PO_0030072), with the frequency 'often'.
